body: From the documentation this seems to be by design, it says `class_name` specifically

This is by design. The global name is the name that is registered in `ScriptServer`. Inner classes are not registered in `ScriptServer`, so you can't retrieve inner class information via [`ProjectSettings.get_global_class_list()`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-method-get-global-class-list) for example.

There is an unexposed method `get_doc_class_name()` that works for inner classes (like `GlobalClass.InnerClass`), but I'm not sure if this is what you need. What do you want to achieve, why do you need a global inner class name? For debugging, serialization or something else?

I have definitely wanted this for debugging (eg. I have a Tag of a specific type that has some more sub-types, and I use these types to determine what kind of tag I'm looking at: `if tag is tSick.FromCaffeine:` is how I want to write my code for example, instead of using string id's. And in this case it makes sense for me to have my specific types of tSick live in the same file so that I'm not lost when looking at inheritance. But that means when I'm debugging I can't tell what the tag is without adding a string id again.

So, for example, I want to write fluff to the game log whenever a tag is added or removed from the player. I check what type of tag it is and generate some text. As I add tags, I want to be notified that I have not handled a specific tag without an assert: bc this is a non-breaking, non-critical feature I'd rather just push warnings. But because I can't get the names of my inner class, I can't identify what specific tag type is missing fluff and/or an explicit call to ignore that tag type in the log.

It's not insurmountable, but it just seems strange that given an object I can check if it `is` something, but I can't get a simple string representation of what it is.

This becomes even more of a hassle when using an addon such as eg. Dialogue Manager, where there's an extra layer of evaluation and I can't just assert or push warnings. I need to communicate back to gdscript via functions that take an object or a string; in both cases (and for the same reason, catching missed types) it would be super helpful to just be able to communicate a string for whatever the class is, inner or not.

It's quite possible I've gone off the deep end and over-engineered this system using types instead of strings, but I like it except when I run into this issue with debugging/identifying missing content. I thought I'd share since you asked what a use case might be :)
